concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: Which of the following acts of the East India Company mandated that selection for civil employees in British Indian territory would be based on the competitive examinations?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act 1853**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1853** was the last Charter Act passed by the British Parliament concerning the East India Company.
 
• This Act introduced an open and competitive system of recruitment for civil services, marking a significant departure from the patronage system.
 
• The Act mandated that civil service positions in the British Indian administration would be filled through a competitive examination process.
 
• The competitive examinations were to be conducted in England, and the system was open to all British citizens, including Indians, although Indians faced significant barriers initially.
 
• The Act reflected growing demands for administrative reforms and efficiency in the governance of British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1793:** This Act renewed the East India Company's charter for 20 years but did not introduce any significant administrative reforms.
 
• **Pitt's India Act of 1784:** It established a dual system of governance, creating the Board of Control to supervise the East India Company’s civil, military, and revenue affairs.
 
• **Charter Act of 1813:** This Act ended the East India Company’s trade monopoly in India, except for trade in tea and trade with China.
 
• **Impact of the Charter Act of 1853:** It was the first step toward introducing a merit-based system in Indian civil services, which was later formalized under the Indian Civil Service Act of 1861.
 
• **Significance of Competitive Exams:** The provision for competitive examinations laid the foundation for modern civil services in India and reflected the influence of liberal ideas of equality and meritocracy.
